title: Queen against a Pawn
description: A pawn on the seventh against a queen: a win against some pawns and a draw against others. Learn which, and why.
source: Every position is dealt fresh and judged by Lichess's endgame tablebase, which is perfect for seven pieces or fewer. These drills need a connection.

drills.name: Win against a centre or knight pawn
drills.goal: They have a centre or knight pawn one step from queening. Win before it gets there.
drills.idea: Check until their king has to stand in front of its own pawn. That costs them a move, and your king uses it to come one square closer. Repeat.
method: Check or pin until their king is forced to step in front of its own pawn.
That blocks the pawn for one move. Use that move to bring your king one square closer.
Repeat the cycle. Each round gains one king move.
Once your king is beside the pawn, take it or give mate.

drills.name: Draw with a rook or bishop pawn
drills.goal: You have a rook pawn or bishop pawn on the seventh against a queen. Hold the draw.
drills.idea: With these two pawns the corner gives stalemate. Their king never gets the free move it needs to approach.
method: Keep your king next to the pawn and the queening square.
Rook pawn: when the queen comes close, step into the corner in front of your pawn. They must let you out or it is stalemate.
Bishop pawn: when checked onto the knight file, go into the corner and leave the pawn. Taking it is stalemate.
Step in front of your pawn only in those corner positions.

drills.name: Random position
drills.goal: A queen against a pawn on the seventh, and you could be on either side. Decide whether it is a win or a draw, then prove it.
drills.idea: Read the position before you move: what is the material, where are the kings, and which method does it call for?
method: Name the position type before touching a piece.
